items.summary: Long-horizon LLM agents interact with their environments through complete assistant turns while generating each action token by token. items.summary: Streaming audio-visual target speaker extraction (AVTSE) is essential for latency-sensitive applications. However, current causal systems face two coupled gaps. items.summary: Generating videos of a specific subject from a few reference images remains challenging when the camera reveals surfaces that are not visible in the input. items.summary: A benchmark is not merely a collection of test questions; it naturally induces an empirical measure over difficulty. items.summary: Looped transformers reuse a shared block of layers to increase computational depth without increasing the number of trainable parameters. They are trained with backpropagation through time (BPTT). items.summary: Agentic services alternate between model inference on clustered GPUs and external tools on distributed CPUs. items.title: RealCLI: Toward a Unified Evaluation of Human-Agent Collaboration for CLI Agents
items.summary: Command-line interface (CLI) agents increasingly execute longer-horizon tasks, yet existing benchmarks either assume that user instructions remain fixed throughout execution or evaluate task outcomes without capturing runtime collaboration quality. items.summary: Computer-use agents (CUAs) are commonly evaluated against fixed task specifications, but users may omit requirements, add constraints, or require approval before consequential actions. items.summary: Producing long-form videos from narration requires interdependent decisions that remain coherent across shots. items.summary: Large language model agents have enabled software development through natural-language interaction, but extending this paradigm to end-to-end game development remains challenging. items.title: A Broader Look into MLLM's Retrieval Heads
items.summary: Locating relevant evidence in long inputs is a core capability of Multimodal Large Language Models. Prior studies attribute this capability to retrieval heads, a sparse set of attention heads that transfer information from the context to the output. items.summary: Evaluating human-AI co-design requires testing whether coding agents can translate real users' multimodal requests into working application revisions. items.summary: Scaling supervised training for working agents requires diverse professional tasks that yield reliable expert demonstrations. items.summary: Learning velocity fields directly in pixel space is difficult and slow. items.summary: Many Indian banks serve customers through FAQ pages and scripted chatbots. Assistants based on language models could respond faster and carry out requests such as blocking a card, but only if they give correct information and follow the bank's rules. items.summary: Humans routinely consume multimodal content, where textual and visual information is naturally interleaved. items.summary: Despite their extensive pretraining knowledge and strong reasoning capabilities, large language models (LLMs) struggle to adaptively gather information in experimental design tasks.
